result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.k_core()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract the k-core subgraph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16974-L17017){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.k_core(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The k-core is the maximal subgraph where all nodes have degree >= k. Iteratively removes nodes with degree < k until all remaining nodes satisfy the condition. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum degree required for nodes to remain in the k-core. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New graph containing only the k-core nodes and edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#6b6e28fe .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph() for i in range(6): g.add_node(label=str(i)) g.add_edge("0", "1") g.add_edge("1", "2") g.add_edge("2", "3") g.add_edge("3", "4") g.add_edge("4", "5") # Get 2-core (nodes with degree >= 2) core_2 = g.k_core(2) # Returns the number of nodes in the 2-core core_2.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0 ``` ::: :::
